description:
Minor, found while diffing the WGSL kernel against its Rust f32 mirror, 2026-08-06. Behaviourally equivalent today; an unenforced invariant.

Rust surface_distance.rs:460 explicitly sorts:
    sort_small_f32(&mut crit[..nc]);

WGSL surface_distance.wgsl:226 does not, carrying only a comment:
    // crit3 is already ascending from collect_real_roots / quadratic fallback.

The comment is CORRECT today: both cubic_real_roots exits return ascending order (sort_roots at wgsl:175, and the quadratic_real_roots fallback which emits min/max at wgsl:200-201). So this is not currently a divergence in behaviour.

It is worth recording because collect_real_roots in WGSL relies on the breakpoint array bp being strictly increasing, and that holds ONLY if crits is ascending. The invariant is load-bearing but enforced on one side by an explicit sort and on the other by a comment. A future change to either cubic exit path breaks the GPU silently while the CPU stays correct.

FIX DIRECTION: either add the explicit sort to WGSL so both sides enforce it the same way, or add an assertion/comment on the Rust side that the sort is redundant -- but make the two agree on WHY the invariant holds.
title: WGSL relies on an unenforced ascending-order invariant that the Rust mirror enforces with an explicit sort

description: The HIGH-fidelity TRISO benchmark (op-6tz.37, examples/triso_gpu_benchmark.rs) wanted graphite but C-12/C-nat is not in the njoy port's well_known_mat MAT/Z/A table (H/O/Fe/Th/U/Pu only), so Nuclide::from_endf("C12") cannot address it by name; the example fell back to H-1. Add carbon (and ideally the graphite S(a,b) thermal law) so a proper graphite-moderated TRISO physics benchmark is possible. Touches njoy-outram-park-fork well_known_mat.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (investigation pass; left uncommitted for maintainer review, bead NOT closed by the agent).

src/acquire.rs well_known_mat now returns (6,12) => 625 and (6,13) => 628. Both MATs were verified empirically, not guessed: read from columns 67-70 of /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ENDF-B-VIII.0/neutrons/n-006_C_012.endf and n-006_C_013.endf. Test acquire::tests::well_known_mat_is_correct extended with both and passes under --release --features net-fetch. cargo check on njoy-outram-park-fork + outram-mc-libs is clean.

Note on the bead title: ENDF/B-VIII.0 has no C-nat evaluation, only C-12 and C-13, so C-nat is not addable.

IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: this only fixes the NEUTRON sublibrary lookup. It does NOT get you graphite S(alpha,beta) — that is a separate ENDF thermal-sublibrary material (tsl-crystalline-graphite MAT=30, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P MAT=31, -30P MAT=32) which well_known_mat and EndfLibrary::neutron_url cannot address at all (neutron_url hardcodes the /n/ sublibrary path). A doc note to that effect was added above well_known_mat. See op-hc2o for the real graphite thermal path.

title: outram-mc/njoy: add carbon (C-12/C-nat) to well_known_mat so from_endf can reconstruct a graphite TRISO moderator
